title: The Biosphere and Biodiversity
seo_title: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: The Biosphere and Biodiversity Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: The biosphere; biodiversity
standard_text: The biosphere is the part of the Earth where life exists; living things need the conditions it provides. Biodiversity is the variety of living things; they are classified into groups such as kingdoms, vertebrates and invertebrates, using their features and dichotomous keys. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 7, Life and Living: The biosphere; biodiversity)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the biosphere, life processes, biodiversity, classifying plants and animals, and dichotomous keys. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are classified by shared features.
key_sub: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not.
body_html:
How to think about it

The biosphere is the thin layer of the Earth where life is found: land, water and the lower atmosphere. It gives living things air, water, warmth and food. All living things carry out the seven life processes.

Biodiversity is the variety of living things. Scientists classify them into groups by their features: five kingdoms (animals, plants, fungi, protists and bacteria); animals into vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals) and invertebrates; plants into flowering and non-flowering plants. A dichotomous key uses yes/no questions to identify an organism.

Example

A frog has a backbone, moist skin and lays eggs in water. Which group is it?

Vertebrate with moist skin

Answer: amphibian

Example

Is a mushroom a plant?

Can it make its own food?

Answer: no, it belongs to the fungi

Common mistakes

  • Thinking whales are fish.
  • Thinking fungi are plants.
  • Thinking spiders are insects.

faq.a: A variety of species keeps ecosystems stable and gives us food, medicine and clean water.

faq.q: Why is the Cape Floral Kingdom special?
faq.a: It has thousands of plant species found nowhere else on Earth, such as proteas and fynbos.

items.q: Which kingdom makes its own food using sunlight?
items.e: Plants are producers.

items.q: Which feature do all insects share?
c: six legs and three body parts
items.e: Spiders have eight legs, so they are not insects.

items.q: An animal is cold-blooded with dry scales and lays leathery eggs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of reptiles.

items.q: Which group are spiders in?
items.e: Spiders have two body parts and eight legs.

items.q: Which group does a crocodile belong to?
items.e: A crocodile is a reptile.

items.q: Which group does a barnacle belong to?
items.e: Barnacles are crustaceans that stick to rocks.

items.q: Which group does a lobster belong to?
items.e: A lobster is a crustacean.

items.q: Which group does an octopus belong to?
items.e: An octopus has a soft body: a mollusc.

items.q: Which group of living things does a moss belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: A painted turtle has dry scaly skin and lays eggs on land. Which vertebrate group is it in?
items.e: Reptiles have dry scales.

items.q: Which group of living things does a starfish belong to?
items.e: Animals feed on other living things and most can move from place to place.

items.q: Which group does a slow worm belong to?
items.e: A slow worm is a legless lizard with dry, scaly skin: a reptile.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria that cause tooth decay belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: Which group does a turtle belong to?
items.e: Turtles have dry, scaly skin and lay eggs on land: reptiles.

items.q: A dichotomous key gives two choices at each step. What do you do?
c: pick the choice that matches the living thing and follow it
items.e: Each step splits the group in two.

items.q: Which group does a horse belong to?
items.e: A horse is a mammal.

items.q: An animal has a head, thorax and abdomen and six jointed legs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of insects.

items.q: A spring peeper lives in water as a tadpole and on land as an adult. Which group is it in?
items.e: Amphibians change from water to land.

items.q: What is biodiversity?
c: the variety of living things in an area
the number of rocks in an area
items.e: More kinds of living things means more biodiversity.

items.q: Which group has a backbone?
items.e: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals have backbones.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A bee is an insect.

items.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
c: to group them by shared features so they are easier to study
items.e: Classification shows how living things are related.

items.q: Is a gecko a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A gecko is a reptile.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the Tasmanian devil belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the wild dog belong to?
items.e: A placental mammal is a mammal whose young grow inside the mother, fed by a placenta.

items.q: Which of these animals is an arachnid?
items.e: A scorpion is an arachnid.

items.q: Which animal is an invertebrate?
items.e: Invertebrates have no backbone.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the red zebra belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Is a woodlouse a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A woodlouse has a hard outer shell and 14 legs: a crustacean, not an insect.

items.q: Is a goldfish a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A goldfish is a fish.

items.q: Is a pigeon a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A pigeon is a bird.

items.q: Is an axolotl a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Axolotls are amphibians that keep their gills.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch?
items.e: The Tasmanian devil is a marsupial.

items.q: Which of these animals is a crustacean?
items.e: A crab is a crustacean.

items.q: Is a tortoise a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A tortoise is a reptile.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.e: A salmon is a fish.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mammal?
items.e: A fox is a mammal.

items.q: Is a whale a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Whales breathe air with lungs and feed their young on milk, so they are mammals.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the common meerkat belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A ladybird is an insect.

items.q: Is a grass a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A grass makes flowers and seeds (grass and wheat have small green flowers).

items.q: An animal has three body parts and six legs. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has three body parts and six legs belongs to the insects.

items.q: Which group of animals does a frog belong to?
items.e: A frog has moist skin without scales, so it belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: An animal has hair or fur. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has hair or fur belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Which group of animals does a stingray belong to?
items.e: A stingray has scales and fins, so it belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which group of animals does a bat belong to?
items.e: A bat flies but has fur and feeds its young with milk, so it is a mammal, not a bird.

items.q: Is a horse chestnut tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A horse chestnut tree makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a butterfly belong to?
items.e: A butterfly has three body parts and six legs, so it belongs to the insects.

items.q: Which group of animals does a monitor lizard belong to?
items.e: A monitor lizard has dry, scaly skin, so it belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: An animal has a pair of feelers (antennae) and three body parts. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has a pair of feelers (antennae) and three body parts belongs to the insects.

items.q: An animal feeds its young with milk. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that feeds its young with milk belongs to the mammals.

items.q: An animal has moist skin without scales. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has moist skin without scales belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: An animal has scales and fins. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has scales and fins belongs to the fish.

items.q: Is a dandelion a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A dandelion makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: An animal lays eggs in water and its young breathe through gills. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that lays eggs in water and its young breathe through gills belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: How many legs does a slug have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Which group of animals does a toad belong to?
items.e: A toad has moist skin without scales, so it belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: How many legs does a crab have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Is a horsetail a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A horsetail does not make flowers. It reproduces with spores.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the tortoise belong to?
items.e: A monotreme is a mammal that lays eggs.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the hopping mouse belong to?
items.e: A placental mammal is a mammal whose young grow inside the mother, fed by a placenta.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria in our gut belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: How does a bird's nest fern reproduce?
items.e: A bird's nest fern is a non-flowering plant. It reproduces by spores.

items.q: Which feature do all vertebrates share?
items.e: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are vertebrates.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch?
items.e: The common meerkat is a marsupial.

items.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
c: to decide which ones are pretty
to organise them into groups by shared features so they are easier to study
to sort them by size only
items.e: Classification shows relationships.

items.q: How does a maidenhair fern reproduce?
items.e: A maidenhair fern is a non-flowering plant. It reproduces by spores.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: gecko, toad, chameleon, monitor lizard?
items.e: The others are reptiles. A toad belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the lion belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: catfish, stingray, toad, seahorse?
items.e: The others are fish. A toad belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Why do scientists use two-part Latin names?
c: Every scientist in the world can use the same name for a species.
items.e: Common names differ from place to place.

items.q: Which group of living things does a mynah belong to?
items.e: Animals feed on other living things and most can move from place to place.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: beetle, cockroach, cobra, mosquito?
items.e: The others are insects. A cobra belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Which group of living things does an earthworm belong to?
items.e: Animals feed on other living things and most can move from place to place.

items.q: Is a rain tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: It makes flowers, which become fruits with seeds.

items.q: What is the scientific name of the lion?
items.e: Scientific names have two parts: genus and species.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: crocodile, guppy, goldfish, stingray?
items.e: The others are fish. A crocodile belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Which group of living things does a bracket fungus belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: A tortoise has fur, lays eggs and feeds its young milk. Which group is it in?
items.e: Fur and milk make it a mammal.
